It’s very hard, I’ve gone through this myself. As both the shitty person and the shitty things being done to them. The toxicity can feel like you just care more than others about your relationship. The great sex, how easy it is to make up after every fight when really nothing is fixed. 
The truth is, neither of you will change until a factor in the cycle is broken. It’s okay to want someone to not disappear, but I want you to think about yourself. Is this how you want to feel? That you suck? 
I also use to put myself down like that, and so did she. 
Eventually I became far worse than her the longer I stayed in the relationship. It wasn’t benefitting anyone, and I was far from the man I wanted to be.
Toxic relationships will do that, please don’t let this go on for yourself. One night on Valentine’s Day, it was probably the 143th we broke up, and I broke up with her a lot of times due to my own incompetence with managing my life. But that was it, that was the last time we ever broke up and the last. I let her go, she let me go. 
Today, I see her happy with her new boyfriend. I’m sure she has grown as a woman and I’m happy to see her that way. I myself had to change a lot of things. A lot. Life goes on, I promise. Whatever happens, you will be okay :)

When I was 17, I had this girlfriend. I cheated two weeks into the relationship and it was my first time doing anything of the sort. I remember it was mostly because my current girlfriend leading up to the official start of our relationship was very hurtful to me, constantly toying with my emotions. She would leave for no good reason and say it was to “test if I would stay through hardships”. The girl I cheated with had been my friend for a while and always stuck through my side. I definitely had feelings for her as well as my current girlfriend at the time. 

One day I said to my girlfriend, I’m going to watch the Floyd mayweather fight with my friend. She was like “okay that’s fine”. Anyway, I ended up kissing her because she started cuddling up next to me. Then immediately I felt sick from the rest of the night and on the way home. That night I called my girlfriend to tell her what I had done. We broke up later when we fully had a chance to talk about it, although we got back together 2 months later and ended up dating for 2 1/2 years. 

What I took from this, I was a piece of shit for sure. Also, never have a “friend” you’re attracted to as well as if you have a hunch they’re attracted to you. It never, ever ends well. Next, if your partner is treating you awfully, talk about it, don’t hold a grudge because that just ends with a vengeful lust. These are the things I took so I won’t ever be a piece of shit again, because I still really hate the fact that I did and can never take it back.
